question: What does the statistics formula reference note say about Bayes' theorem?
answer: The statistics formula reference note states that Bayes' theorem is P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B) [S1] [S2] [S4]

citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 2. Probability Fundamentals Probability measures how likely an event is, on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). For equally likely outcomes, P(A) equals the number of outcomes in A divided by the total number of outcomes. The complement rule states P(not A) = 1 - P(A). The addition rule is P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together, so their intersection has probability zero. Two events are independent when the occurrence of one does not change the probability of the other, so P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B). Conditional probability is P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B), defined when P(B) > 0. Bayes' theorem reverses a conditional probability: P(A | B) = P(B | A) * P(A) / P(B). Example: a disease affects 1% of people; a test detects it 95% of the time (sensitivity) and gives a false positive 5% of the time.

PROBABILITY RULES
Complement: P(A') = 1 - P(A)
Addition: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
Multiplication for independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B)
Conditional: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B)
Bayes: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B)
Law of total probability: P(B) = sum over i of P(B|Ai) * P(Ai)
